completion_data.completion_summary: Landed --task plus a documented pre-commit Containment self-check uniformly across all fifteen implementation-agent phase-commit recipes, exercised the observed undeclared-path defect as a live regression case proving --task alone does not catch it, mechanically audited uniformity across all 21 invocation sites, and recorded the durable git-commit-scoped.sh chokepoint as a coordinated follow-up specification.

memory_candidates.content: A lease/contention mechanism keyed on declared-scope OVERLAP (two or more tasks declaring the same path, e.g. this codebase's git-commit-scoped.sh --task V5 check against specs/.contention-manifest/) is structurally blind to a path declared by NO task at all -- such a path never enters the manifest regardless of flags passed. This is a different predicate from CONTAINMENT (one concrete about-to-stage path tested against one task's own declared file_scope). When a staging/commit surface needs to catch an UNDECLARED path exceeding a task's own scope, Overlap-family mechanisms (leases, contention manifests) cannot do it; only a Containment check against the acting task's own declared scope can. Verified empirically via a live regression: --task supplied, with a real contention-manifest-dependent script, still landed 9 of 10 undeclared-but-staged paths with exit 0 and no warning.

When a guard mechanism must fire mid-dispatch (inside an already-running agent, between its own start and its own postflight), it structurally cannot be sited at a postflight or cycle-plan layer, because artifacts those layers build (e.g. a once-per-cycle contention manifest) are not guaranteed current or even present at that point. The two remaining candidate sites are: inline in the recipe/prompt itself (reachable immediately, but relies on every future author remembering to copy or point at it -- an interim measure at best), or inside the one shared script/chokepoint every recipe already calls (the durable fix, since it cannot be forgotten by a new caller). When auditing fifteen-plus near-identical recipe copies for a missing check, author the fix ONCE in a canonical, named location and have every other copy POINT at it by name rather than duplicating prose -- this avoids per-copy drift and makes a later mechanical uniformity audit (grep for the pointer/block name plus the flag) trivial.
